summary: This lecture discusses the Islamic jurisprudence of wiping over footwear during wudu (ablution), specifically addressing whether the material and style of footwear matters. The speaker explains that based on prophetic traditions and companion practices, there is no distinction made regarding the type of footwear—whether socks (jawrab), shoes (na'al), or leather boots (khuff)—as long as they cover the majority of the foot. The lecturer emphasizes that the focus is on understanding the actual practice of Prophet Muhammad and his companions rather than the various scholarly opinions that developed later across different Islamic schools of jurisprudence (madhahib).
